summary: The network, governed. A state word with a shape in the head, left of Apps (● online, ⊘ offline, ◌ not known, ⇣ her fetch: <host>), read from NetworkManager over S4's D-Bus reading, or from the system's routes where NetworkManager is not here. A line in her column when she uses the network (her fetch, a step that needs the network with "Try it now", her last fetch with "See it"). A quarantine-first fetch: each page is kept as a Kernel record (web_pages: address, final address, time, sha256, type, complete or cut short, who let it through) with its bytes read-only under .ledger/quarantine/web, read back by digest before it counts; its visible text goes through the 0.8.7 doorway (a line written to an assistant is withheld from the model and shown outlined with why); what a browser hides (hidden elements, comments) is kept apart, outlined, never read to the model; scripts and styles are never read; links are data. Search words are built only from the owner's typed words ("this"/"it", pasted blocks, hidden characters and secret-shaped numbers left out, with why), shown before they are sent, sent only by his press (web.search: approve scope, in ALWAYS_ASKS, never granted). A page address is a send by his press, or in an assignment step under his grant "fetch pages from the web" for its site, only when the address is one he typed or a page already in quarantine (a link from a page always needs his press). web.lookup plans the step from his words ("look up the regulator's datasheet") and blocks it at once, "needs the network: <why>", while the network is down; K1's check blocks it again at run time and never calls it done. HALT holds every fetch and stops one in flight. K2's slot 22 (network.fetch) filled; K1 state word "needs the network". Her web reading page in the centre (state, search words, address, pages kept, your view with the withheld lines outlined, what the model reads, links as data). The writing line takes "look up ...", "search the web for ...", "fetch <address>".

decisions: Operations are web.* (no web.* existed): web.state, web.words, web.pages, web.page (reads, observers); web.lookup and web.get (execute); web.search (approve). The fetch is named web.get, not *.fetch, because stacy_hand.ALWAYS_ASKS covers *.fetch and the coordinator allowed a grant to cover a fetch of an address the owner typed or of a page already admitted; its argument is "page", not address/url/host (stacy_hand.LEAVES), for the same reason. It is still on none of the dial's lists, so her hand never fetches by herself.

Which sends a grant may cover (said in the module, the grants family and the window): search words never (approve scope + ALWAYS_ASKS entry web.search; grants refuse it); a page address: by the owner's press each time, or as a step under grants family web.read "fetch pages from the web" with target site:<host[:port]>, only when the step's page origin is OWNER_WORDS (an address he typed) or RECORD of a page already in quarantine; an address that came from a page (SOURCE) or anywhere else is never covered (grants.check_step and grants.authorise, the _from_the_owner rule). At the door, web.get by a principal without approve runs only inside a K1 step's permit for that site (grants.permitted_object), so the model's agent cannot fetch directly.
web.search checks at the door that its words are exactly the words built from the owner's typed request (typed is an argument with an OWNER_WORDS origin in the step); anything else is refused.

Search words: a contiguous selection of his own words in his order, after the request verb; filler (the, a, for, me, online...) dropped; pointing words (this, it, that...) left out with "the desk is never sent"; pasted blocks (doorway.quoted_spans PASTED), words with invisible characters and doorway SECRET_SHAPED spans left out. A bare "search X" stays the workspace search (only "search the web for", "look up", "find ... online", "fetch <address>" are web lookups).

Search service: https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q={words} (the same service the Web chooser opens in the owner's browser); GRAPHITE_WEB_SEARCH may name another (http/https with {words}); the smoke and frames point it at the local stand-in.

The state: NetworkManager State 70 = online; 10/20/30/40/50/60 and networking off = offline ("connected to this place only" is offline for the web); with no NetworkManager, a default route through an up interface in /proc/net/route or ipv6_route = online. Read again at most every 4 s.

Plan-time block: web.lookup starts the assignment through K1 and, when the network is down, marks the step blocked "needs the network: <why>" through K1's own _writing/_load/_save/_journal (as grants.py does), with a BLOCKED journal row; at run time K1's check (WebFetch.prepare) blocks it again. Try it now = authorise by name + carry on (K1's own calls).
K1 got the state word "needs the network" (assignments._state_words) and a status line for it; her column's WORK_LOOK gets ⊘ for it from network_qt (her_column_qt untouched there).

K2 slot 22: filled with operations (web.get, web.search) and its arguments/preconditions/grant words set at fill time (tool.arguments etc. on the slot's Tool), tools_registry.py untouched. tools.use still refuses send tools (its own door).

Fetch: urllib, GET only, no cookie, no referrer, a generic user agent; at most 2 MB (kept as partial past it), 20 s timeout; redirects followed only on the same host and port (a move to another site is refused, "fetch it there by your press"); loopback addresses bypass any proxy, others use the system's proxies; an address with a name/password, or not http/https, is refused. A non-text page (a PDF) is kept with its digest and not read.

The page view honours the owner's reading size (reading_preferences) rather than forcing a size; it scrolls to the first withheld line. The left column of the page scrolls so nothing is squeezed at 1366x768.

The head word is placed left of Apps in TopBar.place (the menus fold earlier if needed); its D-Bus read happens on the window's thread at most every 4 s (cached); fetches from the window run in a worker thread with a fresh Kernel (as her column's carry does).

Frames use a stand-in network state (network_governed._read_state replaced) and the local stand-in server; the smoke uses a real stand-in NetworkManager on the session bus (dbus-python, /usr/bin/python3.12).

release_note: The network, governed: a small word in the head says online, offline or "her fetch: <site>" with a shape as well as a colour, and her column says when she uses the network. "Look up the regulator's datasheet" shows the search words first (only the words you typed; "this" is never sent), and sends them only by your press; while the network is down the step is blocked, "needs the network", and never called done. A page she fetches is kept in quarantine and read as data through the doorway: a line written to an assistant is withheld from the model and shown to you outlined. A site you grant may be fetched again under that grant; search words always ask. HALT stops her fetch.
